This holds with --no-worktree, with --since-my-review, and when a live task already holds the foreign pull request.\u0022,\u0022A pull request in the project\\u0027s own repository, however it was named, opens a lap as it does today, including when the project\\u0027s recorded URL differs from the pull request\\u0027s in letter casing, a .git suffix, or being an ssh remote.\u0022,\u0022The project\\u0027s repository is the one its recorded URL names or, when no URL is recorded, the one gh repo view observes; a mismatch against either is refused as the first criterion says. When neither names a repository, the lap proceeds, matching the daemon\\u0027s guard.\u0022,\u0022Automated tests cover the first four criteria through the command\\u0027s scripted gh and worktree seams, without touching real git or GitHub.\u0022]},\u0022AgentContext\u0022:{\u0022hasValue\u0022:true,\u0022value\u0022:\u0022Hand-off from idea f8212260\\u0027s discovery (its workspace findings.md:185-187), where it was inferred. Settled by reading the code at origin/main 619890054: the daemon\\u0027s guard exists and the command has none. Not run live.\\n\\nShape: one task, one small pull request, not stacked. 71b8826c (a draft about a missing archived-project check in the same method) goes right after the project resolves and this check goes after the pull-request read, so they touch different lines, neither changes the other\\u0027s behaviour, and neither blocks the other.\\n\\nThe daemon refuses this case at both of its checkout sites, before any fetch: src/Hall9k.Daemon/Execution/RunLauncher.cs:243-271 and 1156-1173. Its comment states the hazard: the checkout fetches from the project\\u0027s own origin, so a pull request from a different repository either silently checks out whatever pull request shares that number, or fails with an unhelpful missing-ref error.\\n\\nThe command has no such check, in src/Hall9k.Cli/Commands/PullRequestReviewCommand.cs:\\n- The argument accepts owner/repo#N and URLs (help text, lines 65-70), and GitHubPullRequestSurface.cs:151-158 passes that repository to gh pr view --repo. A bare number passes no repository, so gh answers from the checkout\\u0027s default repository, which in a fork checkout can be upstream while the worktree still fetches from origin. That is why the guard reads what gh returned rather than what was typed.\\n- RunAsync goes straight from the read (lines 139-141) to minting the reference (line 143), then to the adopt and attach arms (lines 148-171). No line compares pullRequest.Repository with the project\\u0027s repository.\\n- Both checkout sites cut by number from project.RepositoryPath (lines 620-621 and 854-856). GitWorktreeManager.cs:209-210 fetches refs/pull/N/head from origin.\\n- The command\\u0027s PrReviewWorktreeRequest passes no head commit, unlike RunLauncher.cs:1193, so nothing notices the mismatch.\\n\\nThe result is a briefing about one pull request over a checkout of another, which is worse than a failure because it reads as a normal lap.\\n\\nPlace the check immediately after the read and before RefuseUnreviewablePullRequest, so that a closed foreign pull request gets this refusal and the check covers adoption and attachment alike. It also applies under --no-worktree, where there is no wrong checkout but the lap would still put a review task on the wrong project\\u0027s board, the hazard the doc comment at lines 239-242 names. A DomainValidationException reaches stderr with a non-zero exit through Program.cs:103-105.\\n\\nCompare owner and repo only, ignoring case, exactly as the daemon does: PullRequestUrls.RepositoryFrom (Hall9k.Connectors, PullRequestUrls.cs:53) on the project\\u0027s URL against pullRequest.Repository. No new helper is needed. Do not use PullRequestUrls.NamesForeignRepository: it also compares hosts, so a project recorded with an SSH host alias (git@github-work:you/project.git, which h9k project add accepts) would have its own pull requests refused. The host needs no check here, because GitHubPullRequestReference.RepositoryFromUrl already refuses anything off github.com. The project\\u0027s URL is project.RepositoryUrl, falling back to GitHubWorkItemProvider.TryObserveRepositoryHostAsync through the same processRunner the read uses, as RunLauncher.cs:256-258 does. RunLauncher.OwnerRepoFrom is internal to the daemon and stays as it is; this task does not switch the daemon over.\\n\\nAccepted consequence: a renamed repository whose recorded URL is stale is refused, even on a bare number, because gh answers with the new name (observed on a renamed public repository) and h9k project set has no option to correct a recorded URL. The daemon already refuses automated reviews on such a project, so only the hand lap changes, and it fails with a clear message. This is parked rather than solved here.\\n\\nRunAsync already takes its gh and git seams as parameters for tests. tests/Hall9k.Tests/Integration/ReviewLapTests.cs has no case for this. Its ScriptedGh (line 1882) answers every call with the same pull-request JSON, so the fourth criterion needs a scripted gh that answers gh repo view separately. The fixture\\u0027s project has a recorded URL, so existing cases never reach the fallback.\\n\\nAdd one clause to the \\u003CPULL-REQUEST\\u003E help text (lines 66-70) and the matching line in docs/cli.md, saying the shorthand or URL must name the project\\u0027s own repository.\\n\\nOut of scope: h9k task add --from-pr still adopts a foreign pull request, and the daemon refuses it at launch with a clear
